page.notes: Public adult-media catalogue. Audited home, listing, category, detail, search, signup and 404 templates. Playback, authenticated account settings, upload, payment and cancellation were not covered because they require media interaction, authentication or commercial commitment.

findings.summary: Loading placeholders continue animating when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion evaluate probe found eight running 2,000 ms placeholder animations and zero accessible prefers-reduced-motion rules while the emulated preference was active.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, stop looping placeholder animation and replace it with a static state or near-instant opacity update.

findings.summary: Navigation uses abrupt full-document swaps without a declared cross-document transition.
findings.evidence: DOM snapshots identify a multi-page site with ordinary links, while route screenshots show independent full loads and no view-transition declaration was present in the rendered document.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an opt-in @view-transition rule for same-origin navigation and stable view-transition-name values for shared header/content elements, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Persistent navigation is sticky but does not adapt to scroll position.
findings.evidence: The categories DOM computed nav as position: sticky with a fixed 40 px height; mobile and desktop captures show the same large two-row header regardless of content depth.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query to compact persistent chrome after scrolling while retaining an obvious way back to the primary navigation.

findings.summary: The cookie prompt obscures the primary content on every fresh page load.
findings.evidence: Desktop, detail, search, signup, and 404 screenshots show a large centered consent panel covering the page before interaction; on the default viewport it occupies most of the usable content area.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the consent surface to the minimum legally required copy, preserve equally prominent choices, and avoid repeatedly covering each route after a decision.

findings.summary: The blocking consent UI is not exposed as a dialog.
findings.evidence: The screenshot shows modal behavior, but the recon probe found no dialog element and no element with role=dialog; keyboard and assistive-technology modal semantics therefore are not inherent.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the blocking consent flow with a native <dialog>, an accessible name, initial focus, Esc policy appropriate to consent requirements, and explicit Accept/Reject controls.

findings.summary: Navigation, promotion bars, side rails and consent chrome crowd the content.
findings.evidence: The desktop and mobile screenshots devote substantial first-viewport area to two navigation rows, a bright age-verification banner, a promotion strip, a permanent category rail, and the consent overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary destinations behind contextual menus, compact promotional chrome, and let the content grid own more of the first viewport.

findings.summary: The desktop layout is forced into a 360 px mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive measured scrollWidth 1,024 px against a 360 px visual viewport, 664 px of horizontal overflow; the screenshot shows the sidebar consuming most of the screen and clipped content.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the mobile-responsive template for narrow visual viewports, remove fixed 1,024 px body/main widths, and use intrinsic grid sizing with minmax() and clamp().

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and many targets are undersized.
findings.evidence: The focus probe focused the first visible link and computed outline: none and box-shadow: none; it also counted 53 visible targets under 24 px in at least one dimension. Lighthouse separately failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible ring and enlarge or space touch targets to at least 24 by 24 CSS px, preferably 44 by 44 for primary controls.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow under a throttled mobile audit.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 10.3 s, LCP 10.6 s and Speed Index 12.5 s (performance score 0.55); the first-party trace also measured LCP 3.58 s, above the 2.5 s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP asset, reduce critical CSS and startup script work, and avoid delaying meaningful content behind consent and initialization code.

findings.summary: The entry page ships a large, script-dominated request graph.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 154 requests and 1,959,472 transferred bytes, including 65 scripts totaling 1,167,373 bytes and three parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets. Lighthouse estimated 26 KiB unused JS and 57 KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Bundle by route and interaction, remove unused CSS/JS, defer nonessential third parties, and reduce the number of critical stylesheets.

findings.summary: Interactive controls have missing or mismatched accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.72 and found two unnamed buttons, two unnamed links, and nine visible-label/accessibility-name mismatches.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon control a concise accessible name and ensure aria-label/aria-labelledby text includes the visible label.

findings.summary: Important text does not meet minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 13 contrast failures, including age-verification copy at 2.15:1 and 1.75:1 and video metadata at 3.29:1, below the required 4.5:1 for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text and surface tokens to meet WCAG AA in every theme and verify the age banner, metadata, and link states with automated contrast tests.

findings.summary: The mobile viewport disables user scaling and the page does not reflow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because the served mobile metadata includes user-scalable=no; the independent 360 px layout test also found 664 px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and restrictive maximum-scale settings, then make all primary templates reflow without two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px and at 200% zoom.

findings.summary: Security headers are absent and three first-party cookies lack Secure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy headers. The cookies primitive found three cookies without Secure, including two SameSite=None cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, a restrictive CSP with frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and justify any SameSite=None use.

findings.summary: The initial load contacts a broad third-party surface before consent.
findings.evidence: The tracker primitive observed 13 third-party origins among 17 total and an active Google Tag Manager request; the HAR recorded 154 requests before any consent choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Block nonessential analytics and advertising requests until opt-in, reduce third-party origins, and proxy or self-host essential static dependencies where practical.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and omits layout dimensions.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 29 of 36 images without dimensions, 13 oversized images, 16 legacy-format resources, eight below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and three images without responsive sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio, select image variants close to rendered size, retain modern formats, and lazy-load below-fold media.
